Keysight Technologies Inc operates within the Technology sector and reported revenue of $1.85 billion for the third quarter ended July 31, 2026, according to [D1]. The company delivered net income of $397 million or $2.30 per share on a GAAP basis while non-GAAP net income was $531 million or $3.07 per share as stated in the filing [D1]. Orders rose sharply year-on-year driven by demand for testing solutions linked to artificial intelligence infrastructure as noted in [D2]. The Communications Solutions Group emerged as the principal growth driver with commercial communications revenue jumping significantly while wireline revenue surpassed wireless revenue for the first time in the company's history according to [D3].

Management raised its outlook for the fourth fiscal quarter of 2026, expecting revenue in the range of $1.930 billion to $1.950 billion which is above the analyst consensus as reported in [D2]. Non-GAAP earnings per share are expected to be in the range of $3.34 to $3.40 compared with Wall Street expectations as described in [D2]. Analysts have set price targets indicating a potential upside from the current trading level as described in [D5]. The company announced participation in upcoming investor conferences including the Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference and the 2026 Truist Technology Symposium as reported in [D6].

The supply environment is less flexible today than a year ago requiring deeper engagement with suppliers to deconstrain production for high-demand new product introductions according to [D3]. Supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue while demand continues to exceed the ability to supply at this point as stated by management in [D3]. Operating margin expanded significantly compared with the previous year reflecting the benefits of stronger revenue and disciplined cost management as noted in [D2]. Free cash flow reached a level providing the company with additional financial flexibility while it continued to return capital through its share repurchase programme as described in [D2].

The research initiative aims to close gap between AI safety research and practical engineering to reduce risk and enable faster, safer deployment of AI-enabled automotive systems according to [D7]. The collaboration will focus on developing practical methods for validating AI systems and generating the evidence needed to demonstrate their safety and reliability as stated in [D7]. This work is designed to enable automakers and suppliers to meet emerging industry requirements while reducing development risk and accelerating the deployment of AI-enabled automotive systems as reported in [D7].
